meta.title: Fungi
meta.subtitle: Medically important fungi: interactive high-yield review

items.text: Mold at 20 °C, yeast at 37 °C (Coccidioides forms spherules in tissue)

children.name: Systemic Mycoses (Dimorphic)
children.notes: Mold in the cold (20°C), Yeast in the heat (37°C). Except Coccidioides (spherule in tissue). All can cause pneumonia and disseminate. Treat local infx with fluconazole/itraconazole, systemic with Amphotericin B.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Macrophage filled with intracellular oval bodies. (Smaller than RBC).

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Mississippi and Ohio River valleys. Found in bird or bat droppings (caves/spelunking).

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Pneumonia with hilar lymphadenopathy (can mimic TB).

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Local: Fluconazole / Itraconazole. Systemic: Amphotericin B.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Broad-based budding yeast. (Same size as RBC).

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Eastern and Central US, Great Lakes region.

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Inflammatory lung disease -> can disseminate to skin and bone.
Verrucous skin lesions (can simulate squamous cell carcinoma).

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Local: Itraconazole. Systemic: Amphotericin B.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Spherule filled with endospores in tissue (Not a yeast!). (Much larger than RBC).

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Southwestern US (California, Arizona). Associated with desert sand, earthquakes, dust storms.

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Can disseminate to bone and skin.

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Local: Fluconazole / Itraconazole. Systemic: Amphotericin B.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Multiple budding yeast appearing as a {buzzword|'Captain's wheel'}. (Much larger than RBC).

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Latin America (especially Brazil). Affects males more than females.

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Local: Itraconazole. Systemic: Amphotericin B.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Dimorphic exception: Forms {buzzword|pseudohyphae and budding yeasts at 20°C}, {buzzword|germ tubes at 37°C}.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Normal flora of GI tract, skin, and female genital tract.

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Oral and esophageal thrush (immunocompromised, asthmatics using inhalers).

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Topical azole (vaginitis). Nystatin, fluconazole, caspofungin (oral/esophageal). Fluconazole, echinocandins, Amphotericin B (systemic).

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Septate hyphae that branch at {buzzword|acute (45°) angles}. Not dimorphic.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Ubiquitous in environment. Produces aflatoxins (associated with hepatocellular carcinoma).

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA): Asthma/CF patients, bronchiectasis, eosinophilia.
Aspergilloma: Fungus ball inside pre-existing lung cavities (e.g., after TB infection). Gravity dependent.
Invasive aspergillosis: Immunocompromised (neutropenia, CGD). Invades blood vessels -> infarction.

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Voriconazole or echinocandins (1st line). Amphotericin B (2nd line).

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Heavily encapsulated yeast. Not dimorphic. {buzzword|India ink (clear halo)} and {buzzword|Mucicarmine (red inner capsule)}.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Found in soil and pigeon droppings. Inhaled into lungs.

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Cryptococcosis meningitis (major cause of death in HIV patients).

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Amphotericin B + Flucytosine, followed by Fluconazole for maintenance.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Irregular, broad, nonseptate hyphae branching at {buzzword|wide (90°) angles}.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Ubiquitous environmental molds. Pathogenic primarily in ketoacidotic diabetic and neutropenic patients (fungi thrive in high glucose/acidic environment).

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Mucormycosis: Inhalation of spores -> fungi proliferate in blood vessel walls -> penetrate cribriform plate -> enter brain.

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Surgical debridement (urgent) + Amphotericin B.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Yeast-like fungus (originally classified as protozoan). {buzzword|Disc-shaped yeast on methenamine silver stain}. Lacks ergosterol.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Transmitted via respiratory route. Most infections asymptomatic unless immunocompromised (HIV CD4 < 200).

details.label: Treatment
details.text: TMP-SMX (prophylaxis and treatment). Pentamidine, dapsone, atovaquone as alternatives.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Branching septate hyphae visible on KOH preparation with blue fungal stain.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Includes Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton.

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Topical azoles (clotrimazole, miconazole). Terbinafine (nails). Griseofulvin (oral for severe/capitis).

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: {buzzword|'Spaghetti and meatballs' appearance} on KOH prep (spores and short hyphae).

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Part of normal skin flora. Degrades lipids.

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Lipid degradation produces acids that damage melanocytes.
Causes hypo- or hyperpigmented skin patches, typically on trunk and back.
More common in hot, humid weather.

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Selenium sulfide topical (Selsun Blue). Topical/oral antifungals if severe.

details.label: Morphology and diagnostics
details.text: Dimorphic. {buzzword|Cigar-shaped budding yeast} at 37°C. Mold with hyphae and rosettes at 20°C.

details.label: Epidemiology and transmission
details.text: Found on vegetation, sphagnum moss, rose thorns. Traumatic introduction.

details.label: Clinical presentation
list: Local pustule or ulcer with nodules along draining lymphatics (ascending lymphangitis).

details.label: Treatment
details.text: Itraconazole or Potassium Iodide (KI). (Mnemonic: 'Plant a rose in the pot(assium) iodide').
